basis: Neuromuscular dysfunction, contractures and pulmonary hypoplasia define the sequence; hypoplasia occurs in 13/13. Cleft palate occurs in 30-79%.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: pulmonary hypoplasia is a defining component of fetal akinesia deformation sequence and occurs in 13/13 reported patients.

basis: An intrinsic phagocyte oxidative-burst defect defines this blood-cell immunodeficiency. Organ infections are separately diagnosed complications.

decisions.haematologic: primary: this is a functional disease of blood phagocytes, with defective neutrophil oxidative burst; the blood-cell mechanism rule applies.

basis: Neural tumors define disease; hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%, cataracts in 81/148, and cutaneous schwannomas in ~60%. Pigment spots alone do not qualify.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: cutaneous schwannomas occur in approximately 60% and constitute direct tumor occupation of skin; this does not rely on cafe-au-lait spots.

basis: Nail dystrophy and chronic respiratory disease define the syndrome. Lymphatic dysfunction is outside the cardiovascular axis; pulmonary hypertension occurs in only 5-29%.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: the axis covers heart and blood vessels, not lymphatic vessels. Lymphedema does not establish blood-vessel disease; pulmonary hypertension is only 5-29%.

basis: Absent major brain structures and cranial vault define anencephaly. Cleft palate and anophthalmia each occur in 1/2 assessed patients; estimates have very small denominators.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: absence of the cranial vault is a defining skeletal malformation of anencephaly, alongside the defining brain defect.

basis: Cerebellar degeneration and sensory neuropathy define disease; hearing impairment occurs in 3/4 and scoliosis/pes cavus in 30-79%. Ocular findings do not establish intrinsic eye damage.

decisions.ocular: none: nystagmus and strabismus can reflect cerebellar dysfunction; reduced acuity in 30-79% lacks evidence of direct ocular disease.

basis: Destructive periodontitis spans the group; keratoderma defines its predominant syndromic forms. CTSC deficiency causes innate antimicrobial dysfunction; skeletal defects are subtype-specific.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: CTSC deficiency impairs neutrophil antimicrobial function and causes an inherited innate immune defect underlying severe destructive periodontal infection.

basis: Brain malformations define disease; contractures occur in 4/6 and clubfoot in 3/3. Eye and cardiac defects each have only 1/1 assessed, insufficient to establish >=30% across the series.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: VSD is reported in only 1/1 assessed; one affected patient among at least six reported cases does not establish a frequency of >=30%.
decisions.ocular: none: ocular abnormalities have only 1/1 assessed annotations; these isolated observations do not establish >=30% involvement across at least six reported cases.

basis: Neuropathy, intellectual disability and congenital deafness define disease. Persistent lower-limb amyotrophy occurs in 80-99% and structural pes cavus in 30-79%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent muscle wasting occurs in 80-99%, with fixed foot deformity in 30-79%; these are intrinsic functional and structural consequences of this syndrome.

basis: An inherited sialic-acid biosynthesis defect impairs platelet sialylation, production and survival. Myopathy is optional without evidence of >=30%; bleeding sites do not establish other organ disease.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the definition establishes impaired sialic-acid biosynthesis causing defective platelet sialylation, an inborn metabolic defect rather than evidence from the gene name alone.
